video_caption: The video segment opens in black and white, showing a large poster featuring a man with a long white beard and long hair, playing a bass guitar. The poster is branded "WARWICK Basses, Amps & Rock'n Roll" at the top, and below the image, it reads "Lee Sklar" along with "The First Carbon-Neutral Company in the Music Industry. Family Owned - Solar Powered - Sustainably Manufactured in a Green Environment". A bald man with a goatee, wearing a white "ISHIBASHI MUSIC" t-shirt and a lanyard, holds a small black recording device and speaks to the camera, gesturing towards the poster. The scene transitions to color, revealing the bald man (Jason) standing next to the actual Leland Sklar, who mirrors the image on the poster with his long white beard and hair, wearing glasses and a dark grey t-shirt, with his arms crossed. Text overlays on the screen identify the speakers: "Jason from ISHIBASHI MUSIC Shibuya, Tokyo" and "Leland Sklar at the Warwick booth, NAMM 2015". Jason engages Leland Sklar in conversation, and Leland Sklar humorously refers to himself and his poster image, saying "Memorex? I don't know, you tell me, which one of us is real?" and then jokes about losing his wristband. The background shows a bustling trade show floor with other booths like "Framus" and attendees walking by.

Two men are engaged in conversation within what appears to be a bustling trade show or exhibition hall. The man on the left is bald with a goatee and wears a white t-shirt featuring a red circular logo with a musical note and the text "ISHIBASHI MUSIC" (Ishibashi Music). He is actively speaking, his mouth open as if laughing or talking animatedly, and holds a small black portable recorder with a microphone pointed towards the other man. A badge on his lanyard reads "JASON". The man on the right, who strongly resembles the person depicted in the large background poster, has long white hair, a very long white beard, and glasses. He is wearing a dark grey t-shirt and has his arms crossed, listening intently with a thoughtful expression. Behind them, a large display features the text "Warwick" and "Basses, Amps", along with an image of a man with a long white beard holding a bass guitar. To the left, another booth displays guitars with the brand name "Framus" visible. A "4400" sign is seen in the distance, and the "ISHIBASHI MUSIC" (Ishibashi Music) logo is watermarked in the top right corner of the video.

The video segment features two men standing indoors, likely at a trade show or exhibition, with a large poster behind them. The man on the left is bald with a light goatee, wearing a white t-shirt with a red "ISHIBASHI MUSIC" logo and a lanyard with a "JASON" name tag. He holds a black portable recorder with a microphone attached, pointing it towards the other man. The man on the right has long white hair and a very long white beard, wearing glasses and a dark short-sleeved shirt with his arms crossed. He appears to be the same person depicted on the large poster behind them, where he is shown in profile with a similar long white beard, playing a bass guitar. The background includes other exhibition booths with musical instruments visible and a blue carpet on the floor. At the 0:10 mark, the text "Selected albums" appears on the left side of the screen, followed by a rapidly scrolling list of musical artists, album titles, and release years, suggesting an extensive discography. This list continues to scroll quickly throughout the remainder of the video segment. At the top right of the screen, the "ISHIBASHI MUSIC" logo is also visible.

Two men are engaged in a conversation in what appears to be an exhibition hall. The man on the left, bald with a ginger goatee, wears a white short-sleeved t-shirt with the red "ISHIBASHI MUSIC" logo and a black lanyard with a badge displaying "JASON". He holds a black microphone and is actively speaking, occasionally looking upwards thoughtfully. The man on the right, with long white hair and a matching long white beard, wears glasses and a dark t-shirt. He listens intently with his arms crossed, his expression thoughtful. Behind them is a large display featuring two identical images of an older man with a long white beard (resembling the interviewee) holding a bass guitar. To the left, another display shows the "Warwick" brand and several guitars. In the background, other attendees can be seen, and a partially visible list-like display shows text such as "Toto - XIV (2015)", "Tanya Tucker", and "Michelle Tumes - Dream", suggesting a context of music artists or albums. The "ISHIBASHI MUSIC" logo is also visible in the top right corner of the video frame.

In an exhibition hall setting, likely a music convention, a bald man wearing a white t-shirt with the red "ISHIBASHI MUSIC" logo (meaning "Ishibashi Music," a Japanese musical instrument retailer) and a "JASON" name tag, interviews an older man with a very long white beard, glasses, and a dark t-shirt, who stands with his arms crossed. The interviewer holds a black Zoom H6 audio recorder with a mic capsule. Behind them is a large promotional poster featuring two profiles of a man with a long white beard holding a bass guitar, presumably the interviewee. Throughout the segment, an inset video in the top left corner displays various clips from a live concert performance under dynamic stage lighting. At approximately 00:14, the text "FALLING IN BETWEEN - LIVE" appears on the inset, followed by the "TOTO" band logo, indicating the concert footage is from a live Toto show. The inset video transitions between wide shots of the stage with band members, close-ups of individual musicians (guitarists, drummer, keyboardist, and singer), and audience shots, all illuminated with vibrant stage lights in blue, red, yellow, and purple hues. The "ISHIBASHI MUSIC" logo is also visible in the top right corner of the main frame.

In a trade show setting, a bald man with a light brown beard, wearing a white t-shirt with "ISHIBASHI MUSIC" (English) in red text, holds a black portable audio recorder and speaks to an older man with a very long white beard, long white hair, and glasses, who is wearing a dark t-shirt and has his arms crossed. The bearded man listens intently and begins to gesture with both hands, palms up, as if explaining something. Behind them, a large poster displays images of the bearded man playing a bass guitar. In the top right corner of the video, "ISHIBASHI MUSIC" and the number "4400" are visible. In the top-left inset frame, a band performs on a brightly lit stage; the view briefly zooms into a close-up of a male singer in a dark suit before returning to the wider band shot.

In a vibrant indoor convention hall, an interview unfolds between two men. On the left, a bald man with a short goatee, wearing a white t-shirt emblazoned with "ISHIBASHI MUSIC" (イシバシ楽器) and a "JASON" name tag on his lanyard, holds a black portable audio recorder close to the interviewee. He attentively listens and occasionally speaks with a focused expression. On the right, an older man with long, flowing white hair, a prominent white beard, and glasses, wearing a dark blue t-shirt, gestures with his right hand while speaking. He looks engaged and thoughtful. Behind him is a large banner featuring a man with a similar long white beard playing a bass guitar, with "WARWICK" and "ROCK & ROLL" text visible. Throughout the segment, a small insert video in the top left corner displays various clips of a band performing on stage under blue lights, showing different musicians playing electric guitar, keyboard, and bass (one shot clearly shows the long-bearded man playing a pink/red bass). The interview covers the interviewee's experience of quickly learning songs for a tour, mentioning a "one-off" corporate event with Lyle Lovett requiring him to learn 35 songs in a couple of days. He also discusses his preference for fan-fretted bass guitars, specifically the Warwick Star Bass, for reproducing low notes effectively, especially when replacing synth bass parts, and how he met Sheldon Dingwall around 15 years prior.

In a well-lit exhibition hall with a blue carpet, a bald man with a goatee, wearing a white t-shirt with "ISHIBASHI MUSIC" (referring to a music retailer) written on it and a matching lanyard, holds a black Zoom H6 audio recorder and converses with an older man. The older man has long white hair and a long, full white beard, wears glasses, and a dark t-shirt; he is gesturing with his hands while speaking. Behind them is a large black poster featuring a younger version of the bearded man playing a brown bass guitar, with text that reads "ROCK 'n Roll." and "Lee Sklar." Below Lee Sklar's name, smaller text states, "The First Carbon-Neutral Company in the Music Industry" and "Green Award - Solar Powered - Sustainably Manufactured in a Green Environment." During their conversation, the bearded man points to a specific area on the bass guitar's body shown in the poster, indicating a damaged section of a bass guitar, explaining that "it's all cracked" and that a seam had "separated" due to airline handling, and that he had used gaffer tape to hold it together. The bald man listens intently, nodding and occasionally speaking.

He has a lanyard around his neck with a visible name tag "JASON" and is holding a black and gray portable audio recorder with a furry windscreen, pointing it towards the other man. On the right, a man with long white hair, a very long white beard, and glasses, wearing a dark t-shirt, is speaking expressively, gesturing with his right hand near the recorder. Behind them is a large black poster with "WARWICK" (partially visible) and "Bass & Rock n Roll." printed on it, featuring an image of a man playing a bass guitar, who bears a striking resemblance to the man on the right. The "ISHIBASHI MUSIC" logo is also present in the top right corner of the video frame.
